spawnData.shape: Single-line top-level JSON array of zone objects {id: string (e.g. 'spawn_686_sheepball'), layerId: string (e.g. 'pal_sheepball'), name: string (display name plus spawner tag, e.g. 'Lamball (green_A_SheepBall)'), mapId: 'palpagos' | 'worldtree', x: number, y: number, radius: number (15000 in all sampled zones)}, in Unreal world coordinates; this matches the description given in the task (53861 palpagos zones, 3474 worldtree zones).
spawnData.palLayerPrefix: pal_ — layerId is 'pal_' + the lowercase InternalName used as the breeder key (pal_sheepball = Lamball, pal_weaseldragon = Chillet, pal_weaseldragon_fire = Chillet Ignis; all three are present with 350, 136 and 73 zones). All 262 distinct layerIds start with 'pal_'. One of them, pal_male_ninjaelite01, is a human/NPC spawner, not a pal.

maps.label: Palpagos Islands
maps.projectionSource: src/lib/coords.ts @ ffe467f: DEFAULT_MAPS.palpagos { worldMinX: -1_099_400, worldMaxX: 349_400, worldMinY: -724_400, worldMaxY: 724_400 } with worldToUv: "const spanX = cal.worldMaxX - cal.worldMinX; const spanY = cal.worldMaxY - cal.worldMinY; const u = (worldY - cal.worldMinY) / spanY; const v = 1 - (worldX - cal.worldMinX) / spanX;" Here span = 1448800, so u = (y + 724400) / 1448800 and v = (349400 - x) / 1448800. Margins and offsets are 0 by default (baseCal). Upstream also comments: "Native map texture size from T_WorldMap / T_TreeMap. MAP_TEXTURE_SIZE = 8192" and "4096 WebP stretched into 8192 CRS", so these fractions apply unchanged to the 4096x4096 image. Sample checks: spawn_57_alpaca (x -289415.2, y 189897.56) gives u 0.631, v 0.441; spawn_686_sheepball (-354643.44, 254394.16) gives u 0.676, v 0.486; spawn_8_weaseldragon_fire (-20924.17, -144309.03) gives u 0.400, v 0.256.
